dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...That's what she told me. Whether it would prove useful or not, I wanted to pass that information on to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The remains... of the Third Descender?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what the Gnoses actually are? Paimon just thought that they looked like chess pieces. How could they be a person's remains?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: All the same, assuming that there was no misunderstanding or special metaphor at play, that is what she meant to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And she said that it would bring "misfortune" and that you should chuck it, which is why you gave it to the Fatui...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If she speaks the truth, then I would simply be putting Fontaine at unnecessary risk by keeping it here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A Descender... She mentioned one of them...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: One, that the Gnoses are related to Descenders.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I had guessed that you might already be familiar with this concept, but I did not expect you to be one of them.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: That means that the Gnoses, which are exceedingly element-compatible and can even enhance elemental abilities, do indeed come from the Third Descender.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Hmm, I wonder... Does your body also possess similar properties?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Like... Uhh, like being able to use elemental powers without a Vision? That does sorta count as special compatibility, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no, let's not think about this stuff right now. It just feels creepy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Comparing {NICKNAME} to the dead Third Descender and all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry, I won't die so easily.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's what you say, but this topic still feels like bad luck.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Once Childe recovers, let's get some more answers out of him — or go look for his Master and get the answers that way!

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I, too, believe it unwise to make too many blind guesses when information is lacking. The same is true of being at court.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Whatever the case, it seems like the crisis here in Fontaine's over for now.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Yes. All of Focalors' efforts were for this moment as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... She sacrificed herself in the end as a god, and she suffered through all those years as a human... Was that really what she wanted?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: ...I suppose that would be the mystery of a god's will.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can you understand the will of the gods?

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: I suspect not. But once in a while, I too would guess that if wishes were like the clouds in the sky, they will one day return to the earth as raindrops...

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: Life flows like water, and rain is the final answer. The water levels may sometimes tilt one way or another, but the rain falls fairly upon all.

response.speaker: Neuvillette
response.text: And what, ultimately, is the difference between the rains that fall upon all of us?

choices.text: For me, this information means two things.
